answer: Sponsor-liability spiral. Each new agent identity must be launched by an existing sponsor who posts a basalt-hard deposit and is contractually liable for that identity's damages. If a clone misbehaves, the sponsor's deposit is seized and their own sponsorship capacity shrinks, forcing a downward spiral of reduced reach. To bridge many clones, an attacker must recruit many sponsors or self-sponsor at escalating deposit rates, making each marginal clone pay more than any expected gain.
